result.summary: Both of this handoff's own assigned corrections are DONE and verified correct in isolation (see 'corrections_applied' below), but the mandated full regression run surfaced a pre-existing, deterministic bug in ELIXIR-DEV's own prior uncommitted §11.9 work (test/support/tenant_template.ex's ensure_template!/0, lines 67-141) that the design's own §11.9.3 predicted could occur and asked TEST-RUNNER's full-suite run to empirically confirm or refute. This run refutes §11.9.3's optimistic empirical expectation: the gap is NOT merely theoretical or rare, it reproduces on every run where an async:false :clone-path caller happens to be the first ensure_template!/0 caller in the VM (before any async:true TenantFixture caller has built/observed the template). Per this handoff's own explicit instruction ('If anything doesn't reconcile, STOP and report a BLOCKER rather than guessing'), this is being reported as a BLOCKER rather than silently patched, since fixing tenant_template.ex is outside this handoff's assigned two-item scope and the design's own §11.9.2 mechanism needs to be re-examined, not guessed at, before a fix is written.

blocker.title: test/support/tenant_template.ex ensure_template!/0's Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call (line 97) fires on the WRONG condition -- gated on template_ready?() (a persistent_term, VM-local flag) instead of on whether the template actually needs building -- causing it to discard an in-flight async:false caller's own uncommitted Tenant insert even when the template is already built in the real database and no build will occur
blocker.reproduction: Isolated to a single, minimal repro (test/letflow/_fk_probe_test.exs, deleted before finishing -- not committed): in a fresh BEAM VM, insert a Tenant via Repo.insert! under the ambient {:shared, self()} sandbox connection, then call Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!() (template_ready?() reads false on this VM's first call, template_built_in_db?() reads true because a real 'tenant_template' schema already exists in the database from a prior mix test invocation) -- immediately after ensure_template!/0 returns :ok, a raw `SELECT id FROM tenants WHERE id = $1` for that same Tenant's id on the same connection returns zero rows: the row is gone. clone_tenant_schema!/1's subsequent Registration insert then fails with Ecto.InvalidChangesetError, errors: [tenant_id: {"does not exist", [constraint: :foreign, constraint_name: "tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey"]}] -- the exact failure signature test-runner's step-05 originally reported across 18-19 files, and the exact ISS-0332 0/5-shape backfill_test.exs regression this whole design exists to fix.
blocker.root_cause: tenant_template.ex:97's Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) is inside the `else` branch of `if template_ready?() do :ok else ... end` (line 69), so it fires on EVERY call where template_ready?() is false -- i.e. every first call per BEAM VM/partition -- regardless of whether template_built_in_db?() (checked later, at line 114, AFTER the mode-switch and advisory-lock roundtrip already ran) will find the template already built and skip the build. Design §11.9.2's own prose (lines 2926-2931 of lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md) describes the intended fix as moving the Sandbox.mode/2 call to fire 'only on the path that is about to actually build the template', but the code as written conditions on template_ready?() -- the wrong, VM-local flag -- not on template_built_in_db?() -- the real, per-call DB check that determines whether a build actually happens. The two conditions coincide only when the template has genuinely never been built anywhere for this database; they diverge, exactly as reproduced here, whenever the template physically exists (built by an earlier mix test invocation, or by a different partition sharing the same steady-state database) but this is still this VM's own first ensure_template!/0 call.
blocker.why_this_exceeds_11.9.3s_disclosed_trade: Design §11.9.3 (lines 2997-3041) already discloses a narrower, related gap -- 'the very first template:clone + async:false call in a given partition/VM, IF it ALSO happens to be the call that triggers the template BUILD' -- and argues this is empirically unobserved in practice because an async:true TenantFixture caller (secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs) already builds the template before the sync queue's first async:false caller runs, per ExUnit's documented 'sync modules run after all async modules complete' ordering (§5.1). That framing implicitly assumes the disruptive Sandbox.mode/2 call only fires on the genuine BUILD path. The bug found here is broader: the call fires on template_ready?()==false regardless of whether a build follows, so it also fires -- with the identical destructive effect -- on a plain STANDALONE run of one async:false-only file (e.g. `mix test test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs` alone, or `mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs` alone), where no async:true caller ever ran first, EVEN THOUGH the template already exists in the database from a prior invocation and template_built_in_db?() will shortly say so. This is a materially larger blast radius than §11.9.3 disclosed and evaluated: not 'the first call in a VM if it's also the build', but 'the first call in a VM, full stop, whether or not a build follows'.
blocker.impact: Every async:false, template::clone TenantFixture caller that happens to run FIRST in its own BEAM VM (any single-file `mix test <path>` invocation touching only async:false TenantFixture callers, and potentially the real full-suite run too if partition/scheduling luck puts the wrong test first) has its own Tenant insert silently discarded, producing the exact ISS-0332/ISS-0113/ISS-0480-class FK-does-not-exist failure this whole rework exists to eliminate. Measured directly across multiple runs this session: test/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill_test.exs run standalone fails 1-4 of its first 4 ISS-0332 tests essentially every time (varies by exactly which test happens to be first); test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs run standalone fails its own first test (C1) the same way. Running two files together in an order that puts an async:true template-builder first (test/letflow/api/context_test.exs + backfill_test.exs) let all 4 ISS-0332 tests pass in one combo run, but a second combo run with a different --seed had ISS-0332's own first test fail instead -- confirming the outcome is genuinely non-deterministic across runs, not merely file-selection-dependent.
blocker.not_fixed_because: Fixing test/support/tenant_template.ex is outside this handoff's assigned scope (two specific doc/assertion corrections named by step-15b's next_action) and outside owned_modules for this handoff. More importantly, the correct fix requires re-deciding a mechanism §11.9.2 already specified in detail (move the Sandbox.mode/2 call inside the template_ready?()==false branch) -- the code already does that literally, and the bug is that the literal instruction itself was insufficiently conditioned (should gate on template_built_in_db?(), not template_ready?(), or restructure to check template_built_in_db?() BEFORE ever touching Sandbox.mode/2). Since a decision record (§11.9.2) already specified 'the fix' and this run demonstrates that specified fix is itself incomplete, CLAUDE.md's 'don't silently re-decide what a decision record already settled' and this handoff's own explicit STOP instruction both point the same direction: this needs CODE-DESIGNER rework (a §11.9.5 or similar correction to §11.9.2's mechanism), not an ELIXIR-DEV judgment call under an unrelated handoff.
blocker.suggested_direction_not_authorized_to_im: The real fix likely needs the DB check (template_built_in_db?()) to run BEFORE any Sandbox.mode/2 call at all -- i.e. restructure ensure_template!/0 so template_built_in_db?() (or an equivalent check) gates the Sandbox.mode(:auto) call directly, rather than gating on the VM-local template_ready?() persistent_term first and only checking the DB state afterward on the assumption that template_ready?()==false implies a build is imminent. This is a design-level decision (whether to add a DB roundtrip before every first-per-VM call, how that interacts with the advisory lock, whether template_ready?()'s cache can be primed from a successful template_built_in_db?() read without also running the build path) that this handoff is not authorized to make unilaterally.

issues.title: test/support/tenant_template.ex ensure_template!/0 (lines 67-141, specifically line 97's Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) placement) discards an async:false caller's own in-flight Tenant insert on every VM-first ensure_template!/0 call, not only on the genuine template-build path -- broader than design §11.9.3's disclosed trade-off
issues.recommendation: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for a §11.9.5-class correction to §11.9.2's mechanism (gate the Sandbox.mode/2 call on template_built_in_db?() rather than template_ready?(), or restructure so the DB check runs first) before this branch can proceed to SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER. This handoff's own two assigned corrections (items 1-2 above) are independently correct and should NOT be reverted -- they fix a real, separate documentation/assertion defect that step-15b's gate already validated the design text for.

result.next_action: STOP. Do not route to SECURITY-REVIEWER. Route to CODE-DESIGNER: rework §11.9.2's mechanism in lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md to correct ensure_template!/0's Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) gating condition (currently template_ready?(), needs to be template_built_in_db?() or equivalent, checked before any Sandbox.mode/2 call) so the disruptive mode-switch only fires on a call that will actually perform the build, not on every VM-first call regardless of whether the template is already physically present. Once CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gates that correction, route back to ELIXIR-DEV to implement the corrected tenant_template.ex mechanism and re-run this same regression suite.
